core.quote: A jack-o'-lantern (or jack o'lantern) is a carved lantern, most commonly made from a pumpkin, or formerly a root vegetable such as a mangelwurzel, rutabaga or turnip.

story.text: 이름은 늪 위에 떠도는 이상한 불빛(도깨비불)에서 왔다
story.quote: Its name comes from the phenomenon of strange lights flickering over peat bogs, called jack-o'-lanterns (also known as will-o'-the-wisps).

story.text: 아일랜드 전설: 사탄까지 속인 구두쇠 잭이 속 파낸 순무 하나만 들고 떠돈다
story.quote: It is suggested that the name also has ties to the Irish legend of Stingy Jack, a drunkard who, after deceiving people throughout his life and even Satan, is doomed to roam the Earth with only a hollowed turnip to light his way.

story.text: 호박 등은 순무 깎던 풍습을 가진 이민자들이 미국에 가져와 해마다 하는 전통이 됐다
story.quote: Jack-o'-lanterns carved from pumpkins are a yearly Halloween tradition that developed in the United States when Celtic influenced immigrants brought their root vegetable carving traditions with them.

items.care: 잭 전설은 설. 순무에서 호박으로 바뀐 이야기로 쓸 것
items.why: 원래는 호박이 아니라 순무였고, 이름은 도깨비불에서 왔다

core.text: 번개 주변 공기는 약 30,000도까지 순간 가열된다
core.quote: The air around the lightning flash rapidly heats to temperatures of about 30,000 °C (54,000 °F).

story.text: 천둥은 급가열된 공기가 만든 충격파 소리
story.quote: Lightning also causes thunder, a sound from the shock wave which develops as heated gases in the vicinity of the discharge experience a sudden increase in pressure.

story.text: 양(+)전하 번개는 드물지만 훨씬 세다(최대 40만 암페어)
story.quote: The average positive ground flash has roughly double the peak current of a typical negative flash, and can produce peak currents up to 400 kA and charges of several hundred coulombs.

items.care: 태양 표면 온도와의 비교는 이번에 연 근거 없음
items.why: 번개 한 줄기 속 공기는 3만 도, 천둥은 그 충격파

core.text: 연필심의 재료는 납이 아니라 흑연이다(연필을 예전에 납 연필이라 불렀다)
core.quote: Graphite pencils (traditionally known as "lead pencils") produce grey or black marks that are easily erased, but otherwise resistant to moisture, most solvents, ultraviolet radiation and natural aging.

story.text: 흑연은 납 광석으로 오해받아 라틴어로 plumbago(납 광석)라 불렸다
story.quote: Consequently, it was called plumbago (Latin for "lead ore").

story.text: 19세기에 흑연 쓰임이 연필 등으로 크게 넓어졌다
story.quote: During the 19th century, graphite's uses greatly expanded to include stove polish, lubricants, paints, crucibles, foundry facings, and pencils, a major factor in the expansion of educational tools during the first great rise of education for the masses.

items.care: 납이 들어 있다고 오해하는 통념 바로잡기

core.quote: The word magnet was adopted in Middle English from Latin magnetum "lodestone", ultimately from Greek μαγνῆτις [λίθος] (magnētis [lithos]) meaning "[stone] from Magnesia", a place in Anatolia where lodestones were found (today Manisa in modern-day Turkey).

story.text: 이름은 자철석이 나던 마그네시아 지방의 돌에서 왔다
story.quote: The word magnet was adopted in Middle English from Latin magnetum "lodestone", ultimately from Greek μαγνῆτις [λίθος] (magnētis [lithos]) meaning "[stone] from Magnesia", a place in Anatolia where lodestones were found (today Manisa in modern-day Turkey).

story.text: 기원전 6세기 탈레스가 자철석이 쇠를 끌어당기는 성질을 처음 알린 것으로 전해진다
story.quote: One of the earliest known references to lodestone's magnetic properties was made by 6th century BC Greek philosopher Thales of Miletus, whom the ancient Greeks credited with discovering lodestone's attraction to iron and other lodestones.

core.text: 파리의 개선문은 나폴레옹의 아우스터리츠 승리 뒤 1806년에 짓도록 명령했다
core.quote: It was commissioned in 1806, after the victory at Austerlitz by Emperor Napoleon I at the peak of his successes.

story.text: 기초만 2년이 걸려 나폴레옹은 새 신부를 맞는 날 목조 모형 개선문 아래로 입성했다
story.quote: Laying the foundations alone took two years and in 1810, when Napoleon entered Paris from the west with his new bride, Archduchess Marie-Louise of Austria, he had a wooden mock-up of the completed arch constructed.

story.text: 프랑스 혁명 · 나폴레옹 전쟁에서 싸운 이들을 기리고 승리와 장군 이름을 새겼다
story.quote: Commissioned to honor those who fought and died for France during the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars, the Arc bears the names of French victories and its generals engraved on its inner and outer surfaces.

items.why: 신부를 맞을 때 완성이 안 돼서 나무 모형으로 대신했다

core.quote: Classic clothing has the button on the left side for women and on the right side for men.

story.text: 고전 복장은 여성은 왼쪽 · 남성은 오른쪽에 단추를 단다
story.quote: Classic clothing has the button on the left side for women and on the right side for men.

story.text: 여성복 쪽은 시중드는 하녀가 오른손잡이라 왼쪽이 편했기 때문이라는 설명이 흔하다
story.quote: For women's clothing the common reason given is that in times when upper-class women's clothing was quite elaborate, servants were needed for dressing, and the left placement of the buttons was more convenient for right-handed maids.

core.quote: A hoodie is a type of jacket or sweatshirt with a hood that, when worn up, covers most of the head and neck, and sometimes the face.

story.text: 후드 달린 풀오버는 1930년대 미국 뉴욕주 추운 창고 노동자용 작업복으로 시작됐다
story.quote: The hooded pullover is a utilitarian garment that originated in the 1930s in the US for workers in cold New York warehouses.

story.text: 1930년대 챔피언(Champion)이 처음 만들어 추위 속 노동자에게 팔았다
story.quote: The earliest clothing style was first produced by Champion in the 1930s in Rochester and marketed to laborers working in freezing temperatures in upstate New York.

story.text: hoodie 라는 이름이 널리 쓰인 것은 1990년대부터
story.quote: The name 'hoodie' entered popular usage in the 1990s.

core.quote: Ballet (French: [balɛ]) is a type of performance dance that originated during the Italian Renaissance in the fifteenth century and later developed into a concert dance form in France and Russia.

story.text: 말은 이탈리아어 balletto(춤 ballo의 작은 꼴)에서 프랑스어로 건너왔다
story.quote: Ballet is a French word which had its origin in Italian balletto, a diminutive of ballo (dance) which comes from Latin ballo, ballare, meaning "to dance", which in turn comes from the Greek "βαλλίζω" (ballizo), "to dance, to jump about".

story.text: 젊은 루이 14세가 직접 발레에 나왔다(륄리와 함께 춤)
story.quote: By February 1653, Lully had attracted the attention of young Louis XIV, dancing with him in the Ballet royal de la nuit.

story.quote: 국가적으로 어머니의 날을 지키게 된 것은 1956년 국무회의의 결정에 따른 것으로, 당시 한국전쟁 이후 어머니들이 양육은 물론 생업에도 책임이 무거워졌기 때문에 이를 위로하고 기리기 위해 '어머니날'을 만들었다.

story.text: 미국은 어머니날과 아버지날이 따로 있다
story.quote: 미국은 매년 5월 둘째 일요일을 어머니날(Mother's day)로, 아버지날(Father's day)은 6월 셋째 일요일로 정해 시행하고 있다.

core.quote: A beret (UK:  BERR-ay, US:  bə-RAY; French: béret [beʁɛ]; Basque: txapel [t͡ʃa.pel]; Spanish: boina [ˈbojna]) is a soft, round, flat-crowned cap made of hand-knitted wool, crocheted cotton, wool felt, or acrylic fibre.

story.text: 프랑스 모자 같지만 바스크 지방에서 대량 생산이 시작됐다
story.quote: Mass production of berets began in the 19th century specifically in the Basque Country, where they were already common headwear among the indigenous population, before spreading to Southern France and the north of Spain; as such, the beret remains associated with these countries.

story.text: 피레네 산맥 양치기의 전통 모자
story.quote: The Basque-style beret was the traditional headwear of Aragonese and Navarrian shepherds from the Ansó and Roncal valleys of the Pyrenees, a mountain range that divides southern France from northern Spain.
